user_query: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
clean_summary: The original query omitted months with no transactions and ignored 'purchase' as a withdrawal, so adding a customer×month cross join with LEFT JOIN and including 'purchase' in the CASE fixed the zero-balance rows and correctly subtracted purchases, yielding the expected result.
database_memories: ENSURE: when calculating monthly customer balances from the transactions table, treat both 'withdrawal' and 'purchase' as negative flows by adding txn_type IN ('withdrawal','purchase') to your CASE expression and to any JOIN or WHERE filters
| CONTEXT: transactions(customer_id, txn_type, amount, transaction_date) must reflect all outflows, not just withdrawals
| WHEN_TO_CHECK: when aggregating transactions by date_trunc('month', transaction_date) and customer_id
SELECT customer_id, date_trunc('month', transaction_date) AS mon,
SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type='deposit' THEN amount WHEN txn_type='withdrawal' THEN -amount END) AS net
SELECT customer_id, date_trunc('month', transaction_date) AS mon,
SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type='deposit' THEN amount WHEN txn_type IN ('withdrawal','purchase') THEN -amount END) AS net

ENSURE: to include months with no transactions in your customer month‐end balances, generate a full set of customer×month combinations via CROSS JOIN and then LEFT JOIN transactions with COALESCE on the sum
| CONTEXT: customers(customer_id) must pair with every month in the reporting range; transactions may be missing for some months
| WHEN_TO_CHECK: when querying month_end_balances or any per‐customer monthly summary
SELECT customer_id, date_trunc('month', transaction_date) AS mon, SUM(amount)
WITH months AS (SELECT generate_series('2022-01-01'::date, '2022-12-01'::date, '1 month') AS mon),
customer_months AS (SELECT c.customer_id, m.mon FROM customers c CROSS JOIN months m)
generic_memories: VERIFY: when you classify rows into positive and negative values in an aggregation, ensure your CASE expression and any row filters reference the same set of categories | PRINCIPLE: mismatched filters and CASE conditions lead to omitted or double-counted data | WHEN_TO_APPLY: any time you assign signs or categories to rows before summing | EXAMPLE_USAGE: If you filter WHERE type IN ('in','out') but only handle 'out' in CASE, you’ll ignore other outflows; instead filter and CASE on the exact same type list.

ENSURE: if you need zero results for missing combinations of keys, build the full key set via CROSS JOIN of dimensions and LEFT JOIN your fact table, then COALESCE aggregated measures to zero | PRINCIPLE: direct aggregation skips missing key combinations, leading to gaps | WHEN_TO_APPLY: anytime you summarize across all values of one dimension against all values of another (e.g., customers × periods) | EXAMPLE_USAGE: To report sales per product per month when some combinations have no sales, generate product×month and LEFT JOIN sales before SUM and COALESCE.

VERIFY: after a LEFT JOIN to produce a superset of rows, always wrap aggregate expressions in COALESCE to replace NULLs with an appropriate default | PRINCIPLE: SUM over no matching rows returns NULL, not zero | WHEN_TO_APPLY: after left-joining a dimension set with a fact table and grouping | EXAMPLE_USAGE: Wrong: SELECT d.key, SUM(f.value) FROM dims d LEFT JOIN facts f ON d.key=f.key GROUP BY d.key; Right: SELECT d.key, COALESCE(SUM(f.value),0) FROM dims d LEFT JOIN facts f ON d.key=f.key GROUP BY d.key.

ENSURE: when calculating monthly customer balances from the transactions table, treat both 'withdrawal' and 'purchase' as negative flows by adding txn_type IN ('withdrawal','purchase') to your CASE expression and to any JOIN or WHERE filters
| CONTEXT: transactions(customer_id, txn_type, amount, transaction_date) must reflect all outflows, not just withdrawals
| WHEN_TO_CHECK: when aggregating transactions by date_trunc('month', transaction_date) and customer_id
| EXAMPLE_USAGE:
Incorrect:
SELECT customer_id, date_trunc('month', transaction_date) AS mon,
SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type='deposit' THEN amount WHEN txn_type='withdrawal' THEN -amount END) AS net
FROM transactions
WHERE txn_type IN ('deposit','withdrawal')
GROUP BY customer_id, mon;
Correct:
SELECT customer_id, date_trunc('month', transaction_date) AS mon,
SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type='deposit' THEN amount WHEN txn_type IN ('withdrawal','purchase') THEN -amount END) AS net
FROM transactions
WHERE txn_type IN ('deposit','withdrawal','purchase')
GROUP BY customer_id, mon;

ENSURE: to include months with no transactions in your customer month‐end balances, generate a full set of customer×month combinations via CROSS JOIN and then LEFT JOIN transactions with COALESCE on the sum
| CONTEXT: customers(customer_id) must pair with every month in the reporting range; transactions may be missing for some months
| WHEN_TO_CHECK: when querying month_end_balances or any per‐customer monthly summary
| EXAMPLE_USAGE:
Incorrect:
SELECT customer_id, date_trunc('month', transaction_date) AS mon, SUM(amount)
FROM transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, mon;
Correct:
WITH months AS (SELECT generate_series('2022-01-01'::date, '2022-12-01'::date, '1 month') AS mon),
customer_months AS (SELECT c.customer_id, m.mon FROM customers c CROSS JOIN months m)
SELECT cm.customer_id, cm.mon,
COALESCE(SUM(t.amount),0) AS net_amount
FROM customer_months cm
LEFT JOIN transactions t
ON t.customer_id=cm.customer_id
AND date_trunc('month', t.transaction_date)=cm.mon
GROUP BY cm.customer_id, cm.mon;
